newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Holec to issue shares with bourse re-launch.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Holec to issue shares with bourse re-launch.

text.p: Electrical components maker Holec Holland NV said on Monday it will issue new shares when it returns to the Amsterdam Stock Exchange later this year.

"The stock market launch will consist partly of floating already existing shares and probably a limited issue of new shares," chief executive Guido Declercq told a news conference, adding the issue would probably increase Holec's share capital by about 20 percent.
The bourse relaunch, originally planned for 1998, will take place in 1997 but it has not yet been decided whether this will be before or after the summer.
Declercq said a majority of the Holec shares will be floated, probably as share certificates without voting rights, and the present shareholders will retain a substantial interest.
The company is now owned by UBS Capital BV, a unit of Union Bank of Switzerland, and venture capital group CINven. Holec's management and staff jointly own a 3.5 percent stake.

Holec was a well-known company on the Amsterdam bourse for decades but it was delisted in 1990 when the then troubled company was taken over by industrial group Begemann. It was bought by its present owners five years later, after the group's high voltage division had already been sold separately.
Holec used 1995 and 1996 to reorganise its operations thoroughly and shed loss-making units. The company now has production units in the Netherlands, Denmark and Australia.
It said it only wanted to produce in markets with enough volume and therefore downgraded its subsidiaries in other countries to sales outlets.
In 1996, the first full year after its turnaround, the company posted a net profit of 24.1 million guilders on turnover of 322.7 million. In 1995, it suffered a loss of 19.7 million.
Declercq expected turnover to grow by some five to six percent in 1997 and saw operating profits growing substantially.
Holec's low and medium voltage divisions are market leaders in the Netherlands and Denmark, but growth prospects are limited in these areas.
It therefore aims to increase its activities in fast growing markets such as Southeast-Asia and Eastern Europe where it intends to join strategic alliances with other partners.
In 1996, it set up a 50-50 joint venture in China with Zhenjiang Electrical Corp which won an order worth several millions of guilders within two months after it started.
Declercq said the Chinese joint venture had already booked follow-up orders and was developing even better than expected.
Holec has also become active recently in growth markets such as the Czech Republic and Poland and in the Middle East.

Financial manager Barend Hess said Holec expected to increase the part of non-Dutch turnover on total sales to about 50 percent within two to three years. In 1996, it generated about 41 percent of turnover outside the Netherlands.
He added Holec aims at raising its operating result as a percentage of sales to at least 11 from 1996's 9.7 percent.
Investments, which totalled some eight million guilders in 1996, are expected to double this year, Hess said.
